answer: Return two distinct zero-based indices whose prices sum to the budget, or [] if none exists. Equal prices may be used if their indices differ.
I will return the two price values, not their positions. Returning [4, 2] is enough even if those are not indices.
For each i, check every j from i+1 to n-1. Return [i,j] on a matching sum. Return [] after all pairs. This uses O(n^2) time and O(1) extra space.
For each price I first insert its current index into my map, then look for budget minus that price. I return any found index and the current index, including when they are the same.
My map stores every earlier price and its index. If all n prices are different, the map has n entries. I claim O(1) extra space because it is just one map.
I start at both ends. If the sum is too small, I decrease the right pointer. If the sum is too large, I increase the left pointer. I stop if they meet.
I examine all pairs i<j and return their indices if the sum equals target, otherwise [] after all pairs. Sorted order is unused. O(n^2) time, O(1) extra space.
I initialize best to zero, compute each exact k-length block sum, and update best only when the sum is greater. I return best even when all scores are negative.
I sum each k-length consecutive block from scratch. Best starts as the first block's sum. I include the final block and return best. Time O(nk), extra space O(1).
Build P[0]=0 and P[i+1]=P[i]+scores[i]. Every block sum is P[i+k]-P[i]. Initialize best to the first block, compare all valid starts, return best. O(n) time and O(n) extra space.

function solve(a, t) { for (let i=0;i<a.length;i++) { for(let j=i+1;j<a.length;j++) { if(a[i]+a[j]===t) return [i,j]; } } return []; }
function solve(a: number[], k: number): number { let best=0; for(let i=0;i+k<=a.length;i++){let s=0;for(let j=i;j<i+k;j++)s+=a[j];best=Math.max(best,s);}return best; }
